editorial:
Picture this: a lovable video game bad guy and his speedy best friend leave their arcade home and dive headfirst into the wild, colorful chaos of the internet. Ralph and Vanellope are on a mission to find a rare replacement part for her broken racing game, but the web turns out to be way bigger and stranger than either of them expected. Along the way they meet helpful netizens, including Yesss, a trend-setting algorithm who knows exactly what goes viral. The whole thing feels like a fast, funny road trip through every website you have ever visited, packed with bright visuals and clever jokes that both kids and adults will catch.

John C. Reilly and Sarah Silverman bring tons of heart to their roles, and the animation looks gorgeous whether you are streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, renting on Apple TV, or watching on 4K Blu-ray. The pacing rarely slows down, though the story does get a little heavy near the end when Ralph faces his own insecurities. Still, the emotional payoff lands well. If you enjoy family-friendly adventures with real feelings and plenty of laughs, this one is easy to recommend. It is a great pick for a cozy movie night with the whole family.
endingExplained: In the final act, Ralph's jealousy and fear of losing Vanellope create a dangerous virus that spreads across the internet and forms a giant, monstrous version of himself. Vanellope and the other netizens help Ralph face his insecurities, and he learns to let his friend choose her own path. Vanellope decides to stay in the online racing game Slaughter Race, while Ralph returns to the arcade. They promise to stay best friends, even from far apart.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves family adventures with heart and humor
